findings.title: Invalidate calendar status after deleting the cache
findings.body: The successful delete mutation only calls the optional onSuccess callback; it never invalidates connectedCalendars. The wrapper passes its optional onChanged prop rather than refetching its own query, so deleting the cache with default props leaves the old timestamp and delete action visible after the success toast. That query also disables window-focus refetching. Invalidate connectedCalendars here, as the disconnect mutation already does.

findings.title: Resolve cache status for in-memory delegated credentials
findings.body: Connected calendars can use negative IDs for in-memory delegation credentials, while their reusable cache entries belong to real database credentials. CalendarCacheRepository.getCachedAvailability explicitly handles this by looking up the cache using userId and key, but this new status lookup only matches credentialId. Such delegated Google connections therefore receive cacheUpdatedAt=null and cannot show or clear the cache even when availability is being served from it. Use the same user-scoped resolution strategy and provide a corresponding ownership-safe deletion path.

findings.title: Preserve the existing selected-calendar input contract
findings.body: Adding updatedAt and googleChannelId as required properties changes the input contract of getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb, including its explicitly retained legacy getConnectedDestinationCalendars export. Callers supplying the previously sufficient externalId, integration, and eventTypeId projections are now rejected by TypeScript. Neither new field is read by this function, and cache status is queried separately, so this creates an unnecessary source-compatibility break. Keep the previous input shape or make these additional properties optional.

findings.title: An empty update does not advance SelectedCalendar.updatedAt
findings.body: Calling updateManyByCredentialId with an empty data object does not update any fields; Prisma also leaves @updatedAt unchanged for empty updates. Consequently, this call does not record successful cache refreshes in SelectedCalendar.updatedAt as its comment promises. Pass an explicit updatedAt value if refreshes should update that metadata, or remove the no-op if only CalendarCache.updatedAt should track refresh time.

findings.title: Resolve the environment file relative to the script
findings.body: ENV_FILE is resolved relative to the caller's working directory, not the script location. Running the normal repository-root command `bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` therefore writes to an .env file above the repository instead of the repository's .env. The script reports success, but the application never receives the tunnel URL and an unrelated environment file may be modified. Derive the repository path from BASH_SOURCE before selecting the environment file.

findings.title: Use an environment-file update compatible with GNU sed
findings.body: The `sed -i ''` invocation uses BSD/macOS syntax and fails with GNU sed on Linux. This branch runs whenever GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL already exists, so subsequent tunnel sessions leave the old URL in the environment file. Because the script ignores the command's exit status, it still reports that the URL was updated, and Google webhook subscriptions can continue targeting the previous tunnel. Use a portable replacement operation and stop if updating the file fails.
